newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Poll shows Argentines glum about economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Argentines glum about economic recovery.

text.p: Almost six out of 10 Argentines think the economy will not recover this year, according to a poll published Monday.

In the poll of 912 people in Buenos Aires, 58 percent responded negatively when asked if they thought the economy would begin to grow again before year's end. Only 20 percent thought growth would resume and 22 percent gave no opinion.

The most educated of those surveyed were the glummest. Only 54 percent of the respondents with just primary education said there would be no growth in 1996, compared to 60 percent of those with secondary education and 65 percent of those with higher education.

Supporters of the governing Peronist Party were the most optimistic, with only 39 percent seeing no recovery. Sympathisers of the opposition Radical Party were 71 percent pessimistic, as were 75 percent of those who voted for the center-left Frepaso alliance.

The poll published in the El Cronista daily was carried out by independent think tank Centro de Estudios Union para la Nueva Mayoria. El Cronista did not say when the study was carried out or what its error margin was.
The government has forecast six percent growth in the second half of this year, with growth for 1996 overall at three percent.
